transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just done your post-surgery check-up. Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or how you're getting on with your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First off, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month. So gentle gardening is fine, but try to avoid anything too physically demanding for now.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice! I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes again?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! It's safe to continue using your eye gel for dry eyes. If you were using it before your operation, you can go ahead and use it again unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you're running low on it, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's good to know, thank you! Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
That's a good question. Some light sensitivity is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens, and if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. 

Are you experiencing just mild sensitivity, or is there pain and redness as well?
transcript.delivered: That's a good question. Some light sensitivity is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens, and if it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time. 

How long has it been since your operation? If your vision is still quite blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks, that helps! It's been about two weeks now, so I'll keep an eye on it. I don't have any more questions at the moment. Appreciate all the information!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! Just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
